daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Asset Forfeiture Bill continues to generate political debate, with DPD member Pigai urging caution in its drafting and warning lawmakers to carefully consider potential negative impacts. Former Coordinating Minister Mahfud revealed that Megawati supports the bill but shares concerns about possible misuse, while he separately explained why the bill was not discussed by the previous DPR period. The MPR claims public response to PPHN is positive, marking another constitutional reform under discussion.

  • In the ongoing haji quota corruption trial, defendant Gus Alex (Yaqut) revealed that 24 DPR members requested money during an official visit to Saudi Arabia in 2024, with each receiving 1,500 riyal per person which he described as "souvenir money," and he also admitted to receiving $85,000 from a travel agency.
  • The Attorney General's Office resumed questioning of Febrie Adriansyah after his pretrial motion failed, with investigators probing a Rp 40 billion payment from businessman Tan Kian to the former official.
  • A Kompas investigation revealed illegal payments from Blueray boss John Field flowing to Customs officials, while the Attorney General's Office questioned 11 witnesses in the MBG case including BGN technical experts and alleged brokers.
  • The Muktamar NU congress resolved that education budgets must not fund the Free Nutritious Meals program, entering the political debate over MBG financing.
  • DPD member Arya Wedakarna was summoned by the DPD Ethics Council and questioned about his attendance at a transgender pageant in Bangkok.
  • Internet service providers voiced support for swift passage of the Cybersecurity Bill currently before the DPR.
  • Partai Ummat is experiencing a political transition, with Kompas reporting the party was previously challenged by cadres and now left by its chairman, marking a new chapter in founder Amien Rais' political vehicle.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo completed his visit to Russia where he attended the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, with Prabowo emphasizing Indonesia's free and active foreign policy at the EEF forum. During bilateral talks, Prabowo apologized to Putin for previously being unable to accept invitations due to domestic matters. The president returned to Indonesia on Thursday evening after concluding the visit.

  • Prabowo promoted Indonesia as a gateway for the Eurasian Economic Union to access the ASEAN market, highlighting that the Indonesia-EAEU FTA opens access to Indonesia's 290 million consumers.
  • Indonesia invited Russian investment in 138 new energy blocks and sees benefits in energy cooperation with Russia, with plans to build a urea fertilizer production facility in Vladivostok.
  • Prabowo pushed for Danantara and a Russia fund to jointly finance infrastructure projects between the two countries.
  • An Indonesian citizen from Depok was found to have become a Russian mercenary after claiming to travel to Malaysia for tourism, raising security concerns.

Other

The government announced a Rp 30 trillion budget cut to the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program for next year, amid ongoing food poisoning cases that have sparked national concern. The National Food Agency head said several MBG poisoning cases have entered the police investigation stage, while in one severe incident 752 students at SMAN 1 Lasem suffered diarrhea, overwhelming the school's toilet facilities. The health minister disclosed that 173 regional hospitals lack seven essential specialist doctors, highlighting gaps in the healthcare system.

  • Forest and land fires continue to worsen, with the forestry minister freezing permits of five companies linked to fires in West Kalimantan, and vowing to fight to protect citizens from the haze, while Kompas reported that fire hotspots have increased, affecting both humans and orangutans.
  • The Solo city government declared a 14-day emergency status after the Putri Cempo landfill caught fire, with authorities planning water bombing operations to extinguish the blaze.
  • State gas company PGN converted 75 vehicles to compressed natural gas, with drivers potentially saving Rp 990 million annually, while fuel purchasers are now required to show vehicle registration documents when buying subsidized fuel.
  • The government prioritized human-centered AI principles for inclusivity in technology policy, while separately integrating STEM education into early childhood programs.
  • An Indonesian-Chinese joint venture established cooperation to build solar panel facilities, and the Bora Pulu plant generates Rp 3.7 billion in annual non-tax revenue for the government.
